title: 航空システム専門実験・演習A
subtitle: Aeronautics Major Lab/Exercises A
educationalGoal: Students will: (1)learn the method and theory of a selected basic subject, and perform experiment and practice on selected subject. (2)acquire deeper understanding and ability to apply engineering subjects. (3)learn how to write the experimental method in an experiment report. (4)learn how to create presentations on experiments and their results.
advice: Students will carry out the following experiments in Exercise A. Details on the experiments can be confirmed in the textbook. ① Molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics) ② Strength evaluation of the thin sheet structure with stiffeners (Semi-monocoque structure) ③ Flight dynamics Students attending the lecture will be divided into three groups (A, B, and C). Group A will carry out experiment ① for five weeks and then theme ② for the next five weeks and finally theme ③ for another five weeks. Group B will follow the order of ②→③→① and group C the order of ③→①→②. In addition, class details are distributed at the time of the start of each experiment theme. It is also important to utilize AI and open data as assistance to own learning.
books: Textbook "Aerospace Major Lab/Exercises AB" published by Kanazawa Institute of Technology
requiredKnowledge: Student should read the textbook before an experiment and understand what kind of experiment they will be carrying out. In addition, students should make a lesson report before a class as preparation, if necessary for that class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to plan an experiment and carry it out independently based on knowledge learned.
Be able to carry out tests safely based on an understanding of the principle of an experiment and the measuremen
Be able to arrange test data using computers and explain the key and problem appropriately.
Be able to reliably interpret the results of an experiment and evaluate the validity of the test data.
Be able to explain the obtained test data reasonably by comparing it with an analytical solution.
Be able to summarize the experimental results in a report, submit it before a deadline, and explain them.

achievementLevels.ideal: ① Students understand the basics of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs) and design CFRPs laminated plates. Students understand the details of the experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording, analysis and consideration of test results. ② Students properly conduct tests of three characteristic buckling types for semi-monocoque structures b evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results. ③ Students can properly explain the generation of lift and the principle of stability, the difference between test models and actual aircraft, and record test data.
achievementLevels.standard: ① Students understand features of the mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs). Students understand experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording and analysis of test results. Students prepare reports and presentations as scheduled. ② Students conduct the buckling experiments and give a general explanation of the buckling phenomena in a presentation. ③ Students can roughly explain the generation of lift and the principle of stability, the difference between test models and actual aircraft, and record test data.

lessons.content: Students understand the learning objectives, outline, and target abilities of this course based on the distributed syllabus. In particular, students understand which role this course assumes within the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and a rough concrete level of achievement. ①Guidance on outline and manner of operation of molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics). Students research design of laminated CFRPs using a prepreg sheet with given properties. Students start to prepare lamination.
lessons.assignments: Students understand the relationship between the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and this course. ①Students research the application, molding method and strength properties of CFRPs, and hand in the research report the following week.

lessons.content: Students laminate prepreg sheets based on a defined design in the first week and make laminated plates by hot press molding.
lessons.assignments: Students research evaluation method of strength properties of CFRPs based on the JIS standards given in the first week.

lessons.content: Students cut out specimens from the molded plates by diamond-cutter and measure the dimensions. Students understand the handling of the universal testing machine. Teaching assistants conduct bending tests and obtain load-deflection curve.
lessons.assignments: Student research strength properties and the calculation method of the strength of the molded plates by load-deflection curve.

lessons.content: Students evaluate the bending properties of the molded plates from the experimental results in the third week, and examine these results and compare them with designed values. Students begin preparation of report and presentation.
lessons.assignments: Students prepare result report, PowerPoint material and presentation.

lessons.content: Students hand in result report and deliver presentation and discussion. Students need to research literature before presentation for proper question and answer. Students self-check the content of the experiments, reports, presentation and attendance.
lessons.assignments: Students rehearse group presentation and prepare presentation by researching literature for question and answer.

lessons.content: Strength evaluation of Semi-monocoque structure Orientation: It is explained that the aircraftstructure consists of thin sheet metal; therefore, buckling strength becomes a problem for structural design. The experimental method and general background of the buckling experiment,including the calculation method of the buckling load, are explained. In addition, actual examples of aircraft structures, T-3 and OH-6D, are shown as the teaching materials.
lessons.operation: Lecture and meeting Confirmation of experimental procedure and task allocation in the experiments.
lessons.assignments: Students should review the three types of buckling typical for semi-monocoque structures from a textbook of structural mechanics. Students should also read p. 5 of the textbook and understand the purpose of the experiment.

lessons.content: Snap buckling test Students can understand the typical failure mode of shell structures though a comparison between a theoretical and experimental buckling load obtained from the snap buckling tests using an aluminum can they prepare. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students review failure behavior of the shell structure and predict the expected failure load and the buckling mode through the textbook pp. 6 to 7.

lessons.content: Shear buckling test Students observe the shear buckling process, such as the shear buckling wrinkle and load resistant capability, under a tension field through the shear buckling test. Students learn the shear load resistant capability of the shear load members of the aircraft, including spar-webs and rib-webs through a comparison between the experimental value and the expected failure load. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should learn tension field theory and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students should also read pp. 7 to 10 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the shear buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Compression buckling test A thin sheet has little load-resistant capability after compression buckling. However, reinforcement with thin stiffeners shows an enhanced load-resistant capability even in a post-buckling situation. Students observe the above state by experiment. At the same time, students also confirm by sight the situation of the structure which caused compression buckling. In addition, students estimate the effective width based on the experimental results and also understand the grounds of the enhancement of strength for the stiffened panel. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students learn the theory of the compression buckling and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students read pp. 10 to 12 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the local buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Oral presentation and report submission Students perform an oral presentation on three kinds of buckling experiments. Using experimental data and a comparison between test results and the theoretical predicted value, students investigate the load resistance capability of the stiffened panels. In the oral presentation, students can appropriately cope with various questions by having researched the reference documents. Self-check of current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should perform preparations for their oral presentation and the submitted report. Students should understand the style of the submitted report by reading pp. 13 to 14 of the textbook and also prepare for questions in the oral presentation by reviewing the related documents for the concept of stiffened panels.

lessons.content: Flight dynamics Equipment: Flight demonstration wind tunnel Flight dynamics test (1): aerodynamic properties Investigation of lift characteristics of the aircraft model as the angle of attack is varied. Comparison between experimental data and theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.

Flight dynamics test (2): trim and neutral points Investigation of static stability and neutral points of the aircraft model as the center of gravity moves. Comparison between experimental data and theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook pp. 36 to 45 Create 2nd report

lessons.content: Flight dynamics test (3): short period oscillation and phugoid oscillation Investigation of dynamic stability of the aircraft model as free flight varies. Comparison between experimental data and theoretical analysis. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
lessons.assignments: Read textbook pp. 46 to 51 Create 3rd report

lessons.content: Flight dynamics test (4): stalling Investigation of stall characteristics of aircraft model using flow visualization. Self-check the content of the lecture, experiments and theory.
Oral presentation and integrated learning Review and self-evaluation
lessons.assignments: Prepare to submit second report and oral presentation. Self-evaluation on achievement in this course.
